meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Class 12 Maths Integration Exercise 7.2 solutions on integration by substitution, with a free 8-question quiz to test yourself.

quiz.title: Integration Exercise 7.2 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on integration by substitution from Exercise 7.2 — spotting the inner function, the f′(x)/f(x) pattern and powers of a bracket. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score. Add + C to every antiderivative.
quiz.about: Integration by substitution (u-substitution); the f′(x)/f(x) rule

questions.explanation: Put u = x², so du = 2x dx. The integral becomes ∫ e^u du = e^u + C = e^(x²) + C. The 2x is exactly the derivative of the inner function.
This is the f′(x)/f(x) pattern: the top, 2x, is the derivative of the bottom, x² + 1. So ∫ f′/f dx = ln|f| + C = ln(x² + 1) + C.

questions.q: ∫ sin x cos x dx equals:
questions.explanation: Let u = sin x, so du = cos x dx. Then ∫ u du = u²/2 + C = sin² x / 2 + C. (Substituting u = cos x gives an equivalent answer differing by a constant.)
Let u = 2x + 1, so du = 2 dx and dx = du/2. Then ½ ∫ u⁵ du = ½ · u⁶/6 = (2x + 1)⁶/12 + C. Do not forget to divide by the 2 from du.

questions.q: For a differentiable f, ∫ f′(x)/f(x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Substitute u = f(x), so du = f′(x) dx. The integral becomes ∫ du/u = ln|u| + C = ln|f(x)| + C. Recognising this pattern saves time in the exam.
Let u = 3x, so du = 3 dx and dx = du/3. Then (1/3) ∫ cos u du = (1/3) sin u + C = (1/3) sin 3x + C.
Let u = ln x, so du = (1/x) dx. The integral becomes ∫ u du = u²/2 + C = (ln x)² / 2 + C.
Let u = x² + 1, so du = 2x dx. Then ∫ u³ du = u⁴/4 + C = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + C. The 2x supplies du exactly, so no extra constant is needed.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.2 of Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It is the integration-by-substitution exercise. You rewrite an integral in terms of a new variable u — usually the 'inner' function — so that its derivative also appears in the integrand. Once in terms of u it reduces to a standard integral from Exercise 7.1.

faq.q: How do I choose the right substitution?
faq.a: Look for an inner function whose derivative is also present (up to a constant). In ∫ 2x e^(x²) dx the inner function is x² and its derivative 2x is right there, so u = x² works. Powers of a bracket, angles inside sin/cos, and denominators are the usual candidates.

faq.q: When can I use the f′(x)/f(x) shortcut?
faq.a: Whenever the numerator is the exact derivative of the denominator, the integral is ln|denominator| + C. For example ∫ 2x/(x² + 1) dx = ln(x² + 1) + C. Spotting this pattern is quicker than writing out the full substitution.

faq.q: Why do I divide by a constant after substituting?
faq.a: If du = k dx, then dx = du/k, and that 1/k factor must be carried outside the integral. This is why ∫ (2x + 1)⁵ dx gives (2x + 1)⁶/12 rather than /6 — the extra 2 from du halves the result. Forgetting it is the most common slip.
